content:
In #36202 (which I was just reminded of), @Yaël Dillies suggested that instead of having results on the Cantor normal form in their own Ordinal.CNF namespace (see e.g. docs#Ordinal.CNF.zero, etc.), that I should move them out into the Ordinal namespace. My original motivation for this namespacing was twofold:

  • It gives a nice place for docs#Ordinal.CNF.coeff and docs#Ordinal.CNF.eval to live. Without the namespacing they'd be named something like cnfCoeff and cnfEval, which just look like namespacing but worse to me.
  • It avoids polluting the Ordinal namespace. Indeed, the Cantor normal form has been a leaf file for nearly a decade.

I'd like for this PR to move forward, so I ask. Is there any rule against creating namespaces for definitions, and other definitions which relate to it? Is it sensible to have this namespace, or should I just comply and rename everything?

The current CNF naming is very unusual (in fact, CNF itself should probably be called cnf and this misnaming is possibly why CNF became a namespace in the first place). How exactly is putting CNF lemmas in the Ordinal namespace polluting? All such lemmas will have cnf in their name somewhere.

Hm. Yeah, I think I'm on your side now.

If we're already fixing names, do we want to keep the cnf name? I think it's quite cryptic, but then again cantorNormalForm is a mouthful and there's some precedent in cfc.
cantorNormalForm isn't nearly as long as continuousFunctionalCalculus, but sure.
cantorNormalForm might still be fine but cantorNormalFormEval and cantorNormalFormCoeff seem like a bit much to me
Well, I'll open a rename PR later
I was anxious about doing that back when I opened #36202 since I had just done another bulk rename of this file but that one has since expired, so
cantorNF is also a good choice. We already have docs#MeromorphicNFAt
